```{r}
# Load CO2 data for test
data(CO2)
```

## 1. Write a function that calculates the ratio of the mean and the median of a given vector.

```{r}
mean_by_median <- function(x) {
  mean(x)/median(x)
}

# Test
mean_by_median(CO2$uptake)
```

## 2. Write a function that ignores the lowest and the highest value from a given vector and calculate the mean. 

```{r}
mean_without_max_min <- function(x) {
  mean(x[-c(which.max(x), which.min(x))])
}

# Test
mean_without_max_min(CO2$uptake)
```

## 3. Read about piping from here:https://r4ds.had.co.nz/pipes.html#pipes. Write a short (max. 300 characters, no spaces) explanation of why, how, and when not to use pipes. 

Pipes pass output of one step to the next, making code more readable by showing workflow left-to-right. Use pipes when transforming data in clear sequential steps. not to use pipes for very short tasks, multiple inputs or outputs, or complex branching.

## 4. Familiarize yourself with the apply-family of functions (apply, lapply, sapply etc.) http://uc-r.github.io/apply_family Write a short explanation (max. 300 characters, no spaces) of why they could be useful in your work. 

I am working for allergy research by studying a large birth cohort with lots of variables, the apply-family of functions can save time, reduce manual errors, and make gene, biomarker, or exposure data processing more efficient and reproducible.
